name: Як уникнути пату
description:
In chess, you can win or lose. But a game can also end in a tie. In chess this is called a draw. Both players get a half point.

How does a game end in a draw? There is more than one way to reach a draw. For instance, when neither side has enough pieces on the board to the checkmate the enemy king. If both White and Black are left with a solitary king, it is a draw.

A chess game can also end in a draw by stalemate. It is very common for beginners. This lesson teaches you what a stalemate is.

Example 1 presents a stalemate:

• It is your turn
• You are not in check
• You can’t move anywhere

If your king can’t move, but one of your other pieces can, it is not a stalemate. The game continues. See example 2.

When you are ahead in the game, you want to win. You don’t want a stalemate! Examples 3 and 4 show you how to avoid stalemate.

What do you have to do?
You are ahead in the game. Avoid stalemate!

examples.text:
It is Black’s turn. He is left with only a king.
But the king can’t go anywhere. Wherever he moves, he moves into check. And that is against the rules.
The king is not in check, so it can’t be checkmate.
It is a stalemate. Both players get half a point.

Black is thrilled. He was afraid he was going to lose the game. White is very sad. He was ahead a whole bunch of pieces.

This shows that getting a lead in a chess game is not enough to win. You have to make good use of your extra pieces.
The game is not over until it is a checkmate!

This position is slightly different from example 1. Do you notice why? Now, Black also has a pawn.
He still cannot do anything with his king, but he can move the pawn. This is not a stalemate.

examples.text:
White is in check. No big deal. He can take the rook. But should he use his king or his queen?

Using the king (red arrow) results in a stalemate.
Black’s king has nowhere to go.
And there are no other black pieces.
So this is a draw.

Look what happens when White uses his queen to capture the rook.
Now, the king has more space. He can actually move.
That is just what White wants.
With the queen out of the way, Black’s king can step forward. Stalemate avoided!
Now, White wins the game. Just click on the play button to watch the moves.

In this example, White does something smart to avoid stalemate.
White is in check. He must take the black queen.
Should he use his king or his pawn?

For the Black king, it makes no difference. But black still has another piece, a pawn.

If the White king captures the queen, it is a stalemate.
The king cannot move and the pawn is blockaded.

If White uses his pawn to capture the queen, things are different!
Now, the black pawn can move! It is not a stalemate.
The game continues.
